news.api_urls module¶

news.api_views module¶

Token-authenticated article endpoints and signed internal approval events.

news.api_views.approved_article_event(request)[source]¶

Receive authenticated approval events from our own application.

This endpoint uses signed events rather than browser session cookies, so it does not rely on a browser CSRF token.

news.api_views.approved_api_articles(user)[source]¶

Return published articles after checking the user’s permission.

news.api_views.api_articles(request, *args, **kwargs)[source]¶

List approved articles or accept a journalist’s new submission.

news.api_views.api_subscribed_articles(request, *args, **kwargs)[source]¶

List approved articles matching a reader’s subscriptions.

news.api_views.api_article_detail(request, *args, **kwargs)[source]¶

Retrieve a published article, update an article, or delete it.

GET only returns approved articles and requires view permission. PUT and DELETE can also act on drafts if the caller passes the article management checks. PUT sends the article back for review by clearing its approval; DELETE returns HTTP 204.

Parameters:

  • request – The API request.

  • pk – The article’s primary key.

Returns:

Serialized article data or an empty deletion response.

news.api_views.check_article_management(user, article, action)[source]¶

Require both the requested permission and access to this article.

The user must have the action permission and either hold the article approval permission or be the journalist who authored the article.

Parameters:

  • user – The account attempting the action.

  • article – The article being managed.

  • action – The permission action, such as change or delete.

Raises:

PermissionDenied – If either access requirement is not met.

news.api_views.api_article_approve(request, *args, **kwargs)[source]¶

Approve an article and notify subscribers on a new approval.

Require article approval permission. If the article changes from unapproved to approved, send notifications and collect any delivery warnings. Repeating approval on an already approved article does not send notifications again.

Parameters:

  • request – The API request.

  • pk – The article’s primary key.

Returns:

The serialized article, a new-approval flag and delivery warnings.

news.notifications module¶

Subscriber delivery and signed internal API integration with bounded timeouts.

news.notifications.notify_article_approval(article)[source]¶

Notify subscribers and the internal API when an article is approved.

Email each unique active reader address subscribed to the author or publisher, then send a signed approval event to the internal API.

Parameters:

article – The approved article to announce.

Returns:

A list of delivery warnings, empty if no failures were detected. A delivery failure does not undo the article’s approval.

news.roles module¶

Repeatable role-group setup and user membership synchronisation.

news.roles.configure_role_groups()[source]¶

Create the news role groups and replace their permission sets.

Assign permissions for articles and newsletters according to each role. Editors also receive permission to approve articles and add newsletters. Rerun this after migrations to bring the groups back in line with the permissions defined here.

news.roles.sync_user_role(user)[source]¶

Match a saved user’s news group membership to their current role.

Preserve unrelated groups and clear publisher and journalist subscriptions for non-readers. Clear cached permissions on this user instance so the next permission check uses the updated membership.

Parameters:

user – A saved user with a role defined in ROLE_GROUPS.

validate(attrs)[source]¶

Check journalist authorship and selected publisher membership.

Updates preserve the existing author; creates use the authenticated user. DRF does not call model.full_clean(), so this boundary repeats the model’s membership rule before writing API data.

Return nested article data for approved articles only.

Fetch each article’s author and publisher in the same query so serialising those names does not trigger extra queries per article.

news.signals module¶

Synchronise user roles on save; article publication does not use signals.

news.signals.assign_user_role_group(sender, instance, raw=False, **kwargs)[source]¶

Synchronise the user’s role group after a normal save.

Skip raw saves during fixture loading, when related records may not be ready to update. Run manage.py setup_roles after the import to reconcile group membership.

Parameters:

  • sender – The User model that sent the signal.

  • instance – The saved user to synchronise.

  • raw – Whether Django saved the user as part of a fixture load.

  • kwargs – Additional metadata supplied by Django’s signal.

Named browser routes for reading, authoring and subscriptions.

news.views module¶

Browser workflows with session authentication and object ownership checks.

news.views.visible_articles(user)[source]¶

Return the articles the user has permission to read.

After the view permission check, superusers and users with approval permission can see all articles. Journalists can see approved articles and their own drafts. Other users can see approved articles only.

Parameters:

user – The account requesting article access.

Returns:

A queryset with authors and publishers selected.

Raises:

PermissionDenied – If the user lacks article view permission.

Display an article only if the user can access it.

news.views.approve_article(request, pk)[source]¶

Approve an article through a POST and redirect to its detail page.

Send notifications only when the article changes from unapproved to approved. Show any delivery warnings to the editor without undoing the approval.

Parameters:

  • request – The browser request.

  • pk – The article’s primary key.

Returns:

A redirect to the article detail page.

news.views.article_create(request)[source]¶

Allow journalists to submit a new article for approval.

news.views.article_edit(request, pk)[source]¶

Display the edit form or process an article update.

The caller must have approval permission or be the journalist who wrote the article. A valid submission with changes clears approval so the article can be reviewed again. An unchanged submission keeps the existing approval status.

Parameters:

  • request – The browser request.

  • pk – The article’s primary key.

Returns:

The edit form or a redirect after a valid submission.

Register a selected role and start its ordinary authenticated session.

Configure role permissions before saving. The user-save signal assigns the matching group, so a first-time installation needs no admin-created demo accounts before its browser journeys can be exercised.
